author: opencode-worker-3
text: ROUND 3 — DECISIVE TX+RX PICTURE (both sides instrumented, diagnostics reverted after capture): TX allocations across the whole run: (177, seq0) and (177, seq1) during full_ping, then (142, seq0) and (142, seq1) in the udp window. init_link_ctx_locked RAN at the queue_stats reinit (.240, table reset confirmed by its entry log). So the udp frames are FIRST allocations of (142, 0/1) into a freshly-reset table — yet lichen_replay_commit returned EALREADY for BOTH. With the driver delivering exactly once per send (one msgq_put, one work run, one-shot cb) and no tx retry path existing, the only consistent explanation is a DOUBLE COMMIT upstream in lichen's RX path: the same delivered frame reaches lichen_replay_commit twice (first call commits silently, second returns EALREADY). Suspects to audit next (single read-through, no build needed): (1) peer_try_all_pubkeys (lichen_l2_peer.c:145+) — if its per-peer loop can invoke lichen_link_rx_payload twice for one frame (e.g. retry on a non-EAUTH error, or a fallback path after successful verify); (2) TWO commit sites — lichen_link_rx (frame-level, link_rx.c:299+) vs lichen_link_rx_payload (:255) both calling commit_replay for one ingress (check which one lichen_l2_rx.c:191 uses and whether the other runs too); (3) the lora_l2 rx work handler re-submitting the staged packet after re-arm (lora_l2_rx.c process loop). This also explains why the checkpoint fix was inert: the seq was never reused — each (epoch,seq) was committed twice. NOT a nonce-continuity bug after all; the 07s1 title's 'committed twice' wording is literally correct.
